RESULT [selftrain]: In-domain, WeedTeacher gains +2.6 mAP@50 and +3.1 mAP@50:95 over its supervised YOLOv8l baseline. Cross-domain, when the unlabelled data came from the new domain, all four SSOD methods gave 'no or limited improvements' over their supervised counterparts.
US [selftrain]: This is the key warning for training on harvested data. Our harvested datasets come from other cameras, fields and years, which is exactly the cross-domain case where teacher-student self-training stopped helping. Incremental rounds that add pseudo-labelled harvested data should expect small or zero gains and must be checked per round against the sealed holdout. That supports the professor's check [note truncated at collection]
CORRECTION [selftrain]: The abstract matches: 19,931 images (8,435 labelled, 11,496 unlabelled), +2.6% mAP@50 and +3.1% mAP@50:95 over YOLOv8l, and 'no or limited improvements' cross-domain. Detail: the in-domain run trains on 10% of the labelled images and tests on the other 90%.
RESULT [weeds]: In-domain, 10% labelled plus 90% unlabelled: +2.6 mAP50 and +3.1 mAP50-95 over supervised YOLOv8l. Cross-domain, all labelled source plus unlabelled new-domain data: all four semi-supervised methods gave minimal or no improvement.
US [weeds]: Warns against the easy version of the loop. Auto-labelling harvested images that come from a different domain (for example OWLv2 pseudo-labels on Kaggle or Roboflow photos) and adding them helps little when the domain differs. Pseudo-labels pay off inside a domain. The rollback check should expect many increments to be neutral, not only harmful.
CORRECTION [weeds]: Confirmed on all points: authors Deng, Lu and Brainard; YOLOv8l; 19,931 images (8,435 labelled from 2021-23 hand-held cameras, 11,496 unlabelled from a 2024 mobile platform); in-domain at 10% labels gives +2.6 mAP50 and +3.1 mAP50-95; cross-domain gives no or limited improvement.
